Hi Elena — thanks for the remittance. We're looking into this. Quick summary from our side: it appears a legacy credit memo (CM-2026-072) created during the September billing migration was applied by the ledger job to INV-9873 when the payment arrived. That credit memo should have been reserved for a contra-revenue adjustment tied to Q3 ARR reclassification, not customer cash application.

I've attached an AR aging snapshot and will propose journal entries to reverse the legacy CM application and reapply the cash to INV-9987. Mina — reviewed the ledger. Confirming: CM-2026-072 was created in the migration window and flagged as 'migration_hold'. The automated cash application rule matched the customer's open balance and consumed CM-2026-072 when the ACH cleared, which moved cash to INV-9873 on the subledger.

Revenue recognition impact: if we reverse CM-2026-072 now, we will pull ~ $18,750 of ARR from the Q3 reclass bucket back into open AR. That amount was previously treated as a contra-revenue adjustment tied to product credits; reversing will shift recognition schedules for 2 revenue contracts. I recommend the following approach: 
- Create JE to reverse CM application on the subledger (JE #proposed attached).
- Post a cash reapplication JE: debit Cash (bank), credit AR for INV-9873 reversal, then apply credit to INV-9987.
- Tag the JEs with reason: 'migration credit misapply — BrightLayer payment 20261104'.

I'll prepare the proposed_journal_entries_1108.xlsx and run the subledger reval in sandbox. If Leadership OK's, we can post on Thursday to minimize month-close disruption.

-Marcus
Director, Financial Systems
